assessment.summary: The two accepted findings support one bounded opportunity to make unsettled reward state an owned boundary for report progress and share issuance; focused local controls are preferred under current constraints.

nonNegotiables: Principal withdrawals remain available while reward settlement is delayed.
The existing staking, Auction, and Yearn tokenized-strategy interfaces remain supported.
assumptions: No measured gas, latency, memory, or storage budget was supplied.
Bounded deposit unavailability is acceptable unless immediate deposit intake is confirmed as a product requirement.

opportunities.title: Own the reward-lifecycle boundary
opportunities.summary: Coordinate report progress and share issuance against one explicit view of claimable, held, auctioned, and returned reward value.
opportunities.diagnosis: GroveCompounder has no single owned rule for unsettled rewards: report can consume attacker-controlled Auction state as a revert condition while deposits mint from reported assets that omit the same reward lifecycle.

evidence.claim: The auction-mode report transfers GROVE and calls kick without tolerating an already-active Auction, so public external state can revert the report.
Deposits mint against report-boundary assets that omit claimable and auction-pending rewards, allowing a late cohort to share old reward proceeds.
Deposit admission, reward claiming, auction initiation, and report accounting each own only a partial lifecycle check rather than a common settlement invariant.

desiredInvariants: A keeper report advances accounting even when the configured reward Auction is already active.
GROVE is transferred only after the strategy establishes that a new auction can start.
New shares are not minted against a reported asset total that excludes a material reward lot earned by the existing supply.
Every unsettled state has an observable recovery transition while principal withdrawals remain available.

options.title: Focused lifecycle controls
options.summary: Skip transfer and kick while an auction is active, continue the report, and block new share issuance while a material old reward lot is unsettled.

findingCoverage.rationale: The active-auction guard and non-reverting deferral are the direct tactical fix and must pass the original pre-kick PoC.
Fail-closed minting until a material old lot is settled preserves cohort ownership, subject to a dust-resistant materiality policy.

tradeoffs.assessment: The known active-auction revert is removed and material stale-priced minting is refused, though distributed checks can drift and a poor dust threshold can be griefed.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run both original PoCs plus fuzzing across claimable, held, auctioned, returned, reported, dust, and shutdown states.

tradeoffs.assessment: Relevant reports and deposit-limit queries gain reward and Auction state reads but no new transaction hop.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Compare gas for no-reward, sub-threshold, active-auction, clean-settlement, and deposit paths against the affected revision.

tradeoffs.assessment: The design needs only bounded lifecycle values and events rather than per-depositor records.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Inspect storage layout and record the exact new slots before deployment.

tradeoffs.assessment: Reports continue through an active auction, but deposits may be intentionally unavailable until cleanup and must not become permanently dust-gated.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Exercise stale Auction, missed keeper, paused staking, public dust donation, and recovery time bounds while asserting withdrawals remain live.

tradeoffs.assessment: Operators need alerts and a runbook for deferred sale and deposit-gate age, but no new service or custody component.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Dry-run alerts and recovery procedures with explicit maximum gate and deferred-sale durations.

tradeoffs.assessment: The existing synchronous interface is preserved; deposits can stay closed while the focused change and checkpoint are deployed.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Test upgrade or replacement deployment, clean-state checkpoint, reopen, shutdown, and rollback on the pinned integration environment.

residualRisks: A future reward path can omit the shared predicate if enforcement remains distributed.
A materiality policy can either permit small dilution or expose deposit availability to dust griefing.
External Auction and reward-price liveness remain outside the strategy boundary.

workPackages: Define a named, dust-resistant unsettled-reward predicate and recovery states.
Make report-time Auction handling non-reverting and idempotent.
Apply the settlement gate to new share issuance without restricting withdrawals.
Add events, monitoring, runbook, PoC regressions, and lifecycle fuzz tests.
acceptanceCriteria: The public pre-kick sequence cannot stop lastReport from advancing.
Late shares receive none of a material pre-entry reward lot after settlement and unlock.
Dust donations cannot hold deposits closed beyond the documented policy.
Withdrawals and emergency withdrawal remain available in every reward state.
migrationNotes: Keep deposits closed until existing rewards are checkpointed and the clean predicate is observed.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Close deposits, preserve withdrawal access, and return to the previous implementation only after any partially initiated reward operation is understood.

options.title: Queued settlement boundary
options.summary: Accept cancelable USDS requests into a queue, advance old rewards through an explicit coordinator, and mint shares only at a clean post-settlement checkpoint.

findingCoverage.rationale: The coordinator treats an active Auction as a waiting state rather than a report exception, but the original report path needs protection during migration.
Queued requests do not receive shares until the old reward epoch is settled; existing direct deposits must remain closed during migration.

tradeoffs.assessment: One state machine owns settlement and mint activation, reducing lifecycle drift while adding queue custody, ordering, and cancellation attack surface.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Model and fuzz every allowed transition, cancellation race, public Auction change, shutdown, and reentrancy boundary; obtain independent review.

tradeoffs.assessment: Deposit request and share activation become separate transactions and may require batching and additional external calls.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure request, cancellation, lifecycle advancement, and activation gas plus end-to-end latency for representative batch sizes.

tradeoffs.assessment: The queue and coordinator retain request, batch, and lifecycle state that the current synchronous design does not store.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure storage slots and per-request state growth, and compare individual versus aggregate queue designs.

tradeoffs.assessment: Deposit intake is isolated from settlement and requests remain cancelable, but activation now depends on coordinator and keeper progress.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Fault-inject missed keepers, stale auctions, paused staking, partial settlement, upgrade interruption, and cancellation under maximum-delay requirements.

tradeoffs.assessment: Operators must monitor queue age, batches, cancellations, lifecycle states, keeper retries, and stuck-fund recovery.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run a capped pilot and incident exercise with dashboards, alerts, and documented stuck-state recovery.

tradeoffs.assessment: A new custody component and delayed-mint interface require UX, integration, rollout, drain, and independent-audit work.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Deploy with intake disabled, shadow state, pilot a capped queue, prove every request can activate or cancel, and rehearse a full drain.

residualRisks: External Auction liveness can still delay queued activation.
The coordinator and queue introduce new custody, ordering, upgrade, and cancellation risks.
A keeper failure can leave requests waiting until cancellation or recovery.

workPackages: Specify lifecycle, queue custody, ordering, cancellation, maximum delay, shutdown, and upgrade invariants.
Implement and formally review coordinator and queue transitions.
Add strategy adapter, monitoring, capped pilot, migration, drain, and rollback procedures.
Complete independent security review before uncapped custody.
acceptanceCriteria: Every request can either mint after a clean checkpoint or cancel without loss.
An active or adversarially pre-kicked Auction cannot revert a report transition.
No queued cohort receives value from a reward epoch that precedes activation.
Maximum delay, throughput, gas, and storage stay within user-approved limits.
migrationNotes: Do not migrate existing shares into the queue; keep direct deposits closed while the new boundary is piloted.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Disable intake, preserve cancellation, drain every pending request, and leave existing strategy shares on the prior withdrawal path.

opportunities.recommendation: Use focused lifecycle controls unless immediate deposit request intake during reward settlement is non-negotiable; choose the queued boundary only with explicit product support for its custody and operational burden.

openQuestions: Must deposits remain immediately mintable or merely requestable during reward settlement?
What materiality threshold resists dust griefing while preventing meaningful reward dilution?
What maximum settlement and deposit-gate duration is operationally acceptable?
Which Auction views and kick policies are guaranteed across supported deployments?
